subject: Cascade partner architecture checkpoint: reference deployment & validation plan
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Nick Porter <nick@cascade.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Cascade partner architecture checkpoint: reference deployment & validation plan

Nick —

Following up from the kickoff this morning. I attached a first-cut reference diagram and a validation matrix that maps Redwood serving features to the scenarios Cascade indicated (multi-tenant ingestion, near-realtime reranking, and batch embedding refresh). Highlights and asks: 

- Reference deployment: single-region VPC peering + dedicated routing to a subset of models (v1/v1-quant). Diagram includes subnet + NAT patterns.
- Test plan: a two-phase validation (smoke functional tests, then load/latency sweep). Matrix has suggested endpoints, payload sizes, and SLO targets.
- Data flows: we need a short-lived sample dataset and an API key for a non-prod tenant so we can exercise prefix caching and KV warmup.
- Security constraints: Cascade requested an audit log export cadence; we proposed weekly CSV for initial validation.

Can you confirm a non-prod hostname & the SRE point of contact? Also please flag any redlines in the attached diagram (cascade-reference-diagram.v1.pdf). If all looks good we can schedule the validation week the week of May 10.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Partner Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
attachments: cascade-reference-diagram.v1.pdf, cascade-validation-test-matrix.xlsx
From: Nick Porter <nick@cascade.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@cascade.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Cascade partner architecture checkpoint: reference deployment & validation plan

Thanks, Soojin — this is exactly the level of detail we wanted. A few quick notes: 

- Non-prod hostname: api-staging.cascade.ai (we'll issue a scoped API key that expires in 30 days).
- SRE contact: Lydia Chen (cc'd) will own the connectivity and can provision the key.
- Security: weekly audit CSV is fine for now; compliance will later ask for direct S3 export (we'll surface that during procurement).

On the diagram: can you expand the annotation for the KV cache warmup step? We have an internal concern about the cache pre-population latencies during burst windows. Also, for load testing, can you confirm the maximum concurrent streams Redwood expects per vGPU in the dedicated pool?

We can target May 10 as validation week; Lydia and I will reserve time.

—Nick
Nick Porter
Head of Integrations | Cascade Analytics

Nick / Lydia —

Thanks for the quick turn. Answers inline and an updated ask list: 

- KV cache warmup: we added a step to the diagram and the matrix (row 3). Operationally we'll upload a set of representative prefix sequences during the warmup window and exercise a small ramp (5 -> 50 concurrent sessions) to observe hit-rate and tail latency. We'll document the expected warmup duration per model variant.
- Concurrent streams per vGPU: for the v1-quant variant we recommend planning for 8 concurrent high-priority streams per A100-like vGPU (with continuous batching enabled) and up to 24 for lower-priority, batched jobs. We noted these numbers on the diagram.

Action items for Cascade: provide API key + a sample message queue (or S3 bucket) with ~10k sample records by May 6.
Action items for Redwood: produce a short runbook for the warmup step and a smoke script for functional verification.

Marissa — can you review the diagram's updated annotations and sign off on the runbook draft? Karthik — once Marissa signs off, can you enumerate any dedicated capacity sizing constraints we should call out for procurement?

I'll sync with Lydia mid-next-week to confirm times.

Best,
Soojin
